scope: Theorem 1.1 (Exact attainment of zero order) of the manuscript “Exact orders and invariant anticanonical linear systems” (preprints/Exact-orders-and-invariant-anticanonical-linear-systems-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 068 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f93f24f5a8ef95cf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With X, L, α, ν, G0, ℓ as above, let v be either a discrete valuation of C(X) centered on X or the zero valuation. Let M be any fixed line bundle. Suppose that effective integral divisors Nj and positive integers mj → ∞ satisfy Nj ∼ mjL + M, ℓ(Nj) = 0, v(Nj) mj −→ 0. There is an effective rational divisor N ∼Q L such that v(N) = 0.
